tests.description: Validate structured project state, requirement/test references, local documentation links, upstream provenance, and project-tool unit tests. This is repository validation only.
From two clean checkouts, reproduce pinned Rocket and NOVA-baseline RTL elaboration and simulator builds; compare declared artifacts and preserve versions, warnings, resource limits, and exclusions.
Execute declared ISA, exception, and MMU tests with a pinned reference model where supported; detect injected mismatches and record unsupported extensions and exclusions.
Verify two distinct expected harts each execute assigned workloads and reach bounded completion; reject hart-0-only or four-hart-only test coverage.
Exercise simultaneous boot, repeated reset, per-hart interrupt delivery, traps, and bounded recovery under concurrent workloads.
Compare generated device tree and address map against configured memory regions, permissions, cacheability, alignment, and device ownership.
Stress dirty-line exchange, eviction, false sharing, simultaneous atomics, LR/SC, and forward progress across both harts with deterministic seeds and timeout diagnostics.
Run declared memory-ordering litmus and release/acquire message-passing tests; compare allowed outcomes against the chosen architectural model.
Rebuild firmware and Linux images, boot repeatedly, enumerate both harts and devices, schedule work on each hart, and test concurrent load and reboot recovery.

Compare baseline and one original CPU change with identical workloads, inputs, toolchains, memory models, and correctness checks; publish distributions, regressions, and relevant area/timing estimates.

Compare integrated accelerator kernels and an end-to-end inference workload with software-reference results using declared data types and tolerances; cover randomized shapes, overflow, and boundaries.
Verify accelerator command completion, dirty-buffer ownership, backpressure, invalid accesses, reset interruption, and timeout recovery in the NOVA integration.
Execute submitted kernels through the integrated GPU bridge and driver, check results against references, and exercise invalid commands, faults, completion, and bounded recovery.

Validate CPU-to-accelerator-to-CPU transfers under dirty caches and concurrent traffic using the declared coherent or explicitly managed noncoherent contract; include partial transfers and transaction-ID pressure.
Verify all claimed firmware, debug, memory-translation, and DMA isolation boundaries with unauthorized accesses and hostile descriptors; explicitly report absent protections.
On the named physical board, record bitstream hash, FPGA part, tool versions, resources, timing closure, memory tests, boot logs, both-hart execution, and repeated fault/reset recovery.
Review clock/reset domains and crossings with constraints and tool reports; exercise reset sequencing and asynchronous-interface recovery for the chosen implementation.

Validate declared clock/power-state transitions and state-retention rules, then evaluate power using a documented estimation or measurement method; keep FPGA, ASIC estimate, and silicon evidence separate.
Validate the selected physical memory controller/PHY and I/O implementation against its approved technology or board constraints, calibration, error handling, and sustained data-integrity tests.

Reproduce the selected technology-specific synthesis and physical flow with pinned PDK/library/macros, constraints, timing corners, equivalence approach, and explicit DRC/LVS/DFT/power-integrity gaps.
Independently review the selected release profile, required gates, reproducibility artifacts, requirements coverage, unresolved issues, dependency licenses, and scoped capability claims.

For a research-only release, explicitly record that fabrication is not authorized. For an actual fabrication proposal, separately review authorized IP, foundry access, signoff ownership, packaging, test, budget, and logistics; research-release approval cannot substitute for that decision.

requirements.title: Preserve upstream notices and pinned dependency provenance
Maintain traceability and offline foundation checks without hardware qualification claims
Reproduce the unmodified Rocket and named NOVA baseline builds
Verify supported instruction and exception behavior against a declared reference
Verify every heterogeneous hart, interrupt delivery, boot, and reset recovery
Publish and verify the elaborated address and cacheability map
Verify coherence, atomic forward progress, and architectural memory ordering
Reproduce firmware and Linux boot with both harts and matching device descriptions
Evaluate original CPU performance changes with matched baselines
Verify integrated Gemmini numerical behavior and end-to-end results
Verify accelerator memory ownership, completion, faults, and recovery
Validate the integrated GPU and limit graphics claims to tested workloads and APIs
Specify and verify coherent or explicitly managed noncoherent accelerator transfers
Qualify every advertised boot, debug, translation, and DMA isolation boundary
Validate the physical FPGA profile, close timing, and review clock/reset crossings
Validate physical memory and I/O interfaces instead of substituting simulation models
Validate implemented power-state controls and separate estimation from measurement
Reproduce technology-specific implementation and expose all signoff gaps
Release only a reviewed profile with complete reproducibility and evidence records
Keep fabrication authorization separate from a research release
